title: Anyways, go see Cats:The Jellicle Ball if you’re able to- it’s the be...
transcript: Is Broadway broken? This is a question that I've seen posed a lot lately, especially in the wake of Jellicle Ball announcing a closing date. But even just zooming out from Cats The Jellicle Ball for a second, it does seem like we have more and more shows closing faster than they ever have. More and more shows not recouping. And the ones that do recoup are taking longer and longer to do so. So, Is Broadway broken? Well, it certainly seems to not be in a great place right now. Shows are getting more and more expensive to produce, ticket prices are getting higher and higher, and the only thing that seems to be a sure thing right now are celebrity driven plays. And I wish I could give you an easy answer of how to fix it, but unfortunately it's just not that simple. Like, I wish that I could tell you, hey guys, just go support the new original art. The art that is taking bold, creative risks because that has just become financially infeasible for so many people. And it's also not as simple as just lower the ticket prices, because as I said, shows are getting more and more expensive to produce, and those costs have to be recouped somehow. Nor is it as simple as just saying, well, shows should just have better marketing, whatever that means? I do think it is fair to say that Broadway has struggled to bring in new audiences, especially For shows like Jellicle Ball that aren't necessarily being created for your traditional Broadway audiences. But again, is that because of marketing, or is that because ticket prices are astronomical? Probably a little bit of both. I just don't know what the answer is. But it is incredibly disheartening to see shows like the Jellicle Ball close when they open to rave reviews Won some Tony's. Feel perfectly timed for this specific moment in time. And if a show like that can't run for longer than five months, then, yeah, I think Broadway is broken.
